title: How to create pyspark docker image?
question:
When i go through the docker images uploaded for pyspark from docker hub, I see that the last upload was done almost 2 years ago. https://hub.docker.com/r/apache/spark-py/tags

I want to create a new image based on the new spark versions which have come up in the past 2 years. I went through the github code for spark : https://github.com/apache/spark

But couldn't really get my head around how to create pyspark docker image from this, for example for 3.5.4 ?

Please let me know if the question needs more details.
answer:
Hope this Dockerfile helps you:

Just run docker build -t pyspark:latest .

FROM ubuntu:22.04 AS base
MAINTAINER "demir.samuel@outlook.de"

ARG spark_version="3.4.1"
ARG delta_version="2.4.0"
ARG openjdk_version="17"
ARG python_version="3.10"
ENV workdir="/myworkdir"

# Set WorkDir
WORKDIR $workdir

RUN apt update && apt install -y openjdk-${openjdk_version}-jdk && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install Spark
RUN \
    apt update && \
    apt install -y wget && \
    wget https://archive.apache.org/dist/spark/spark-${spark_version}/spark-${spark_version}-bin-hadoop3.tgz && \
    tar xvf spark-${spark_version}-bin-hadoop3.tgz && \
    mv spark-${spark_version}-bin-hadoop3/ /opt/spark && \
    export SPARK_HOME=/opt/spark && \
    export PATH=$PATH:$SPARK_HOME/bin:$SPARK_HOME/sbin && \
    export PYSPARK_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3 && \
    rm spark-${spark_version}-bin-hadoop3.tgz

# Install Python in new layer to improve rebuilds with different versions
RUN \
    apt update && \
    apt install -y python${python_version} python3-pip && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Copy Requirements
COPY requirements-dev.txt .

# Install Python Dependencys
RUN \
    pip install -r requirements-dev.txt

The requirements-dev.txt file looks like the following:

# with this project (e.g. for testing or useful development tools).
# The regular project dependencies are defined in requirements.txt

pytest~=7.2

You can use this image in pycharm. You need to edit in the run configurations the mounting paths. If you want to verify if the image works, just create a container and run some little python script with spark.
